description: mathlib's module-system conversion means non-`public import`s are no longer re-exported, so files silently lose names they used to get transitively. Symptoms are 'unknown tactic', 'unknown namespace', 'Unknown identifier' and dot-notation resolving to the wrong namespace (e.g. `Submodule.inertiaDeg'` when `Ideal.inertiaDeg'` is simply not imported). Fix is an explicit import, not a rename.

before_code: have hIJ_le : I * J ≤ I := Ideal.mul_le_right
after_code: have hIJ_le : I * J ≤ I := Ideal.mul_le_left
description: `Ideal.mul_le_left` and `Ideal.mul_le_right` swapped meaning: they are now `I * J ≤ I` (needing `[I.IsTwoSided]`) and `I * J ≤ J` respectively, matching the general `mul_le_*` convention. DANGEROUS: a blind sed is wrong because sites whose goal happened to match the new reading still compile. Fix only the sites that error; the tells are 'Application type mismatch' and, when the ideal is a metavariable, 'typeclass instance problem is stuck' from the new `IsTwoSided` argument.

`List.TFAE.out` is now 1-indexed to match the `tfae_have` tactic's numbering; passing 0 fails with the bespoke error 'TFAE indices start at 1.' plus a confusing 'could not synthesize default value for parameter' from the `l[i-1]? = some a := by rfl` autoparam. Every index shifts by one.

`isIntegral_algebraMap_iff` dropped its explicit `Function.Injective (algebraMap A B)` argument in favour of a `[FaithfulSMul A B]` instance. Call sites that passed the injectivity proof positionally now fail with 'Function expected at'. Usually no replacement hypothesis is needed since mathlib has the instance (e.g. `FaithfulSMul R K` for fraction rings).

`Subgroup.Commensurable H K` is now `H.IsFiniteRelIndex K ∧ K.IsFiniteRelIndex H` where `IsFiniteRelIndex` is a one-field class, rather than a conjunction of `relIndex ≠ 0`. So `constructor` no longer exposes the arithmetic goals (needs `⟨⟨?_⟩, ⟨?_⟩⟩`) and a commensurator membership proof is consumed via `.relIndex_ne_zero`. `commensurator` also now uses `MulAut.conj g • H` rather than `ConjAct.toConjAct g • H`.

before_code:
theorem sectionPoleSheaf_cartier_away_overlap_generator_isUnit ... := by
  ...  -- (kernel) deterministic timeout under v4.34.0-rc2
after_code:
set_option maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
theorem sectionPoleSheaf_cartier_away_overlap_generator_isUnit ... := by
  ...  -- unchanged; measured 1,817,319 heartbeats with `set_option Elab.async false` + `#count_heartbeats in`
description: Lean v4.34.0-rc2 (lean4#14806) replaced the kernel's union-find is_def_eq cache (transitive closure) with a per-pair cache; rfl/convert-heavy checks over Scheme/SheafOfModules structures then exceed 200k heartbeats even though mathlib needed no adaptation. `(kernel) deterministic timeout` counts elaboration + kernel heartbeats (wrapAsync adds the elaboration count into the kernel task); rejected declarations are re-added as axioms when possible, so `(kernel) unknown constant` cascades hit only some dependents — re-measure dependents with the culprit stubbed. Statement-preserving fix where the total is finite: a measured per-declaration `set_option maxHeartbeats N in` (PoleSheafWeierstrassOverlap 3.2M, PoleSheafModel 1.6M, ProjectiveSpaceTwist:1400 400k).

before_code:
theorem chartTransitionIso_swap_right ... :
    let D := Scheme.GlueData.ofAffineIntersectionFunctor F hopen hpush
    ... := by
  dsimp only
  simpa only [Functor.mapIso_inv] using unitCompExit
    ((Scheme.GlueData.ofAffineIntersectionFunctor F hopen hpush).t i j) ...
after_code:
intro D h
  simpa only [Functor.mapIso_inv] using unitCompExit (D.t i j) (D.t j i ≫ D.f i j) h
description: When a statement binds `let D := <abbrev application>`, `dsimp only` proj-reduces `D.t`/`D.f`/`D.U` into the structure's field bodies while the lemmas used still carry the unreduced projections; under rc2 the kernel re-derives those mixed-form defeqs inside deep ≫-composites without bound (3.2M heartbeats not enough). Keeping `D` let-bound (`intro D`) and stating helper facts in `D`-form makes the abbrev never unfold: both InvertibleSheafGlueData proofs went from a 9463 s timeout to a 160 s green module at the default budget.

description: The rig's build_command builds only lakefile defaultTargets; both real breakages lived in uncovered libraries. Four ProjectiveSpaceTwist theorems run away in memory under rc2 (40–57 GB, hours) under every budget and four proof shapes although every isolated step is cheap — heartbeat caps do NOT bound memory, so run such experiments only under an RSS watchdog. Resolution by human decision: wire the module + 148 dependents out of the library root (52 imports, documented note, lists in .mathlib-quality/bump-pst-*.txt) and file a dev ticket; main green by explicit omission.

# first full-tree build: 17 errors in 5 modules, 'Picard/InvertibleSheafGlueDataDescent' absent
# -> treated the 17 as the complete error inventory
after_code:
# after repairing Picard/InvertibleSheafGlueData, re-ran the FULL tree build:
# Picard/InvertibleSheafGlueDataDescent compiled for the first time on this pin and
# showed the same rc2 kernel pathology, worse (chartTransitionPullHom_comp > 6.4M heartbeats)
description: A failing module truncates its dependents out of the build, so the first build's error list is a LOWER bound, not the inventory: modules behind a broken one never compile and hide their own fallout. Repairing Picard/InvertibleSheafGlueData let Picard/InvertibleSheafGlueDataDescent compile for the first time on the new pin, where it hit the same lean4#14806 kernel blow-up but past every budget. Re-run the full-tree build after each repair and treat the bump as unfinished until a build produces zero NEW modules, not merely zero errors.
